rows.quote: To identify genetic instruments for plasma protein levels, we used the results of genome-wide protein quantitative trait locus (pQTL) mapping for 2,922 unique proteins performed by the UKB-PPP consortium.15 These analyses were restricted to the subset of the UKB-PPP who were of EUR ancestry and selected at random from the UKB (n = 34,557) rather than on the basis of phenotype (as previously described15).
rows.reference_quote: Sun B.B., Chiou J., Traylor M., Benner C., Hsu Y.-H., Richardson T.G., Surendran P., Mahajan A., Robins C., Vasquez-Grinnell S.G., et al. Plasma proteomic associations with genetics and health in the UK Biobank. Nature. 2023;622:329–338. doi: 10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6.
rows.coder_note: Rule E: the pQTL mapping is attributed to reference 15 (Sun 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6) and the sentence gives the randomly selected EUR subset, n = 34,557, the sample size of the discovery row alone; the 28,008 unrelated individuals used for fine-mapping are a subset, not a conflict (rule H).
